messages:
maya: Heads up — eu-west3 is getting hammered after the A/B test rolled. We have a big spike in inference traffic and the autoscaler is not stabilizing. Nodes are being requested but end up NotReady. Latency is up. Anyone digging in?

raj: On it. Do we have the nodepool id and recent events?

thomas: Pasting raw from the cluster: 
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep eu-west3
gpu-node-a-1   NotReady   1/1     <none>   10m   <none>   192.168.12.11   eu-west3-a   A100
gpu-node-a-2   NotReady   1/1     <none>   9m    <none>   192.168.12.12   eu-west3-b   A100
gpu-node-a-3   Ready      1/1     1        2h    <none>   192.168.12.9    eu-west3-c   A100
```
Events on a failed node: 
```
Aug 10 15:02:31 kubelet[1234]: E0910 15:02:31.123 kubelet.go:234] failed to start container runtime: driver init failed: nvidia driver not found
Aug 10 15:02:34 cloud: Created instance gpu-node-a-2 (PROVISIONING)
Aug 10 15:03:02 cloud: Instance gpu-node-a-2 (RUNNING)
Aug 10 15:03:05 kubelet: Node NotReady: kubelet not ready (driver init)
```

lia: That matches my suspicion — we rolled a node-image patch last night that updated the GPU driver and kernel modules. The new image seems to be missing the vendor kernel module for our A100 image on cos-custom variant in eu-west3. Other regions have fallback images, eu-west3 uses the new group.

ops-bot: [cloud] Instance gpu-node-a-4 created in zone eu-west3-b (id: i-0f2b).

raj: Two things to confirm: 1) Are these spot/ephemeral instances getting evicted? 2) Are node-init scripts failing to install the NVIDIA drivers?

thomas: Instance lifecycle from cloud shows rapid creates and deletes for the nodepool: 
```
2026-08-10T15:02:31Z CREATE i-0f2b (gpu-a100, image=cos-custom:v2026-08-09)
2026-08-10T15:03:40Z TERMINATE i-0f2b (evicted: driver-init-failed)
2026-08-10T15:04:12Z CREATE i-0f2c (gpu-a100, image=cos-custom:v2026-08-09)
2026-08-10T15:05:02Z RUNNING i-0f2c
2026-08-10T15:05:10Z kubelet: failed to load nvidia modules
```

lia: Yup — driver-init-failed. The node-init systemd unit that loads the kernel module times out and exits. The autoscaler sees the node as NotReady and keeps requesting more to hit the desired capacity => provisioning churn.

maya: Not great. Traffic keeps queuing. We need a short-term mitigation to stop thrash and a longer fix for the image. Suggestions?

raj: Immediate: 1) Increase nodepool max to allow warm healthy nodes elsewhere (eu-west1). 2) Temporarily exclude eu-west3 from the routing policy so new traffic tilts to other zones/regions. 3) Pause autoscaler or bump scale-up cooldown to avoid infinite creates.

thomas: I'm already scaling up eu-west1 reserve: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize --size=40 ig-eu-west1-gpu` (doing now).

lia: I'll rollback the node-image in the nodepool to previous working tag `cos-custom:v2026-07-28` and trigger a controlled rolling update (maxSurge=1). That should stop new nodes from failing.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Node-image rollout started for nodepool gpu-pool-eu-west3 -> target image cos-custom:v2026-07-28.

maya: While lia does the rollback, let's also mark the broken nodepool as unschedulable so autoscaler doesn't continue to target it. `kubectl cordon nodepool-gpu-eu-west3` (or temporarily set the cluster routing policy).

raj: Quick patch commands: 
```
# cordon the pool (taint all current nodes to avoid new pods)
kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=gpu-eu-west3 -o name | xargs -I{} kubectl taint nodes {} node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable=true:NoSchedule
# slow down autoscaler (set scale-up cooldown to 10m)
kubectl -n kube-system edit configmap cluster-autoscaler-config
# -- set scaleUpCooldown: 600
```

thomas: After cordon I see fewer provisioning attempts. Network metrics show traffic shifting to eu-west1 as desired. Latency improving but still elevated because queued work is draining.

lia: Rollback completed on the image tag and a controlled replace of nodes is in progress. We should see Ready nodes in 8-10 minutes as kubelet starts cleanly with the older driver.

maya: Cost question — we just spun a bunch of on-demand instances in eu-west1 to cover the spike. Should we convert any to reserved or is this purely transient?

raj: For now transient. We can reclaim once load settles. We'll review whether we should pre-warm a small multi-region warm pool (2-4 nodes per region) for canary A/B to avoid cold starts next time. That has a steady cost but reduces risk.

thomas: Observability notes: autoscaler events show repeated scaleUp requests every 30s due to the NotReady window being < scaleDown delay. We should tune thresholds so that NotReady due to driver-init counts as a terminal failure for that instance class to avoid loops. Filing an infra task after this.

ops-bot: [incident] Incident created: #INC-2026-149 eu-west3 GPU driver image rollback + autoscaler churn. Severity: P2.

maya: Good. TL;DR action list: 
- lia: rollback + validate node image (in progress)
- thomas: keep eu-west1 warm and monitor traffic shift (done)
- raj: throttle autoscaler (scale-up cooldown + taint nodes) and update configs to avoid rapid churn
- maya: follow up on warm-pool proposal and cost analysis (postmortem item)

lia: Will post logs from the init scripts here after validation.

thomas: Seeing new Ready nodes in eu-west3 after rollback. Latency trending down to normal.

maya: Nice. Keep this thread for the postmortem notes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
